lines: Somewhere far off, a music box starts its tune again.
The music box tune reaches you in pieces, skipping every few notes.
A carousel creaks around in the dark, its horses rising and falling.
An old radio murmurs from a room with the door shut.
A record skips on a turntable somewhere past the stairs.
Stuck in one groove, the needle repeats the same bar.
Music rolls out of a cracked speaker, then cuts to hiss.
A carnival tune wheezes from a far tent, slow and warped.
Every horse on the merry-go-round groans as the ride slows.
Something turns in the dark with a rusty, patient squeal.
Winding down, a music box drags one note after the next.
Back to its start the tune loops, with a tiny click.
Through the vent comes the thin sound of a radio playing nothing.
A speaker in the next room hums with a faint, wavering tone.
Old dance music seeps through a wall, muffled and wrong.
Bells chime from a toy box until the battery dies.
Wheezing organ pipes on the carousel run a little flat.
A steam organ coughs somewhere up the ramp, then picks up the tune.
Tinny music leaks from a cheap player left on a bench.
A record player turns with nobody near it, the arm hovering.
Static hisses from an old set, then a thin melody breaks through.
The music box stutters, and the room goes still to listen.
Down the corridor, a tune plays slower than it should.
Gears grind somewhere under the carousel, then catch speed again.
A carnival band plays two bars, then the power dips and it stops.
A broken radio clicks through the static, searching for a station.
Hitching and skipping, a record repeats one small note.
Somewhere below, a turntable spins up and goes quiet.
Across the hall, a music box starts up again, thin and far.
Its little comb of metal teeth sounds once more, then stops.
The carousel stops, and the last horse swings slowly to rest.
Wind-up toys tick in a drawer, all of them running down.
Something plays a chord on an organ, then lets it ring out.
Mid-song the radio drops out, and static swallows everything.
A faint hum of a melody rises from the drains, then fades.
A gramophone horn wheezes in an empty office down the hall.
Across the record, a needle drags with a sound like tearing paper.
A music box tumbles off a shelf and plays on in the dark.
Each carousel horse makes its own creak as the platform turns.
Brass music from the carnival floor comes in waves, then drops.
A distant jukebox thumps, loud for a second, then goes dead.
Muffled from inside a locker, the music box tune sounds far away.
Every so often the music box catches up on a missed note.
Turning again, the carousel brings the music back with it.
Soft clicking gears keep time with the box's tune.
A horn blares once over the speakers, flat and tinny, then cuts out.
The tape recorder in the back room winds, stalls, and winds again.
A reel of old tape hisses on a spool that nobody has touched.
Clicking on by itself, the radio fades to a low drone.
Nearby, a speaker crackles with a voice from the relay room.
A low alarm tone warbles through the pipes, then stops.
The lights dim with a faint whine, and the music stutters down.
The outage cuts the music box mid-tune, and the hall goes black.
Its motor coughs, catches, and the carousel turns on again.
A cuckoo clock chirps from somewhere above, out of step with everything.
Chimes ring out from the stairwell, a slow tune played on steel.
A child's music box plays in an empty nursery, then goes silent.
Down in the corner, a phonograph speeds up, then drags to a crawl.
A save point hums quietly, its chime drifting under the carnival tune.
Quiet now, the music box leaves its tune hanging in the air.
A ceiling speaker crackles, and the carousel music slips out of time.
Tapping rhythm drifts through the vents, almost like a song.
Across the field, the ride's whistle shrieks once, then falls silent.
Old carnival lights hum, and a stubborn tune crawls up the stairs.
Held too long, a single note drones from the speaker on the wall.
A hand-cranked music box grinds out a tune from the next block.
Someone is cranking a box somewhere far off, and the tune skips.
Speeding, slowing, speeding again, the record player cannot decide.
A tin whistle plays a few notes in the stairwell, then quits.
Paused, the carousel lets its horses drift in the stillness.
Each time the radio hiss rises, a voice fades in and out.
The speaker in the locker room plays a warped waltz, slow and wide.
A turntable under a dust sheet keeps turning, slow and quiet.
Far below, music seeps up a shaft, too faint to name.
One more time the box plays its tune, and the whole room listens.
